correctness.summary: The lattice resolvent kernel follows from the exact second-order recurrence. Its self-convolution simplifies to a closed form whose combination 2R^2-R has strictly positive coefficients for all s>0. Absolute summability justifies periodization to finite cycles, and commutativity gives C^k R^m=(CR)^k R^(m-k) for m>=k. Exact two-by-two multiplication supplies the Dirichlet counterexample. A compact deterministic verification reproduces these identities numerically.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical Crank-Nicolson/Rannacher smoothing, positivity-preserving Pade smoothing, exact CN positivity bounds, composition monotonicity, and recent rational-map positivity were checked using both terminology and the algebraic composite (I-sL)(I+sL)^(-2). No checked source supplied the exact positive infinite/periodic lattice kernel, its m>=k consequence, and the Dirichlet obstruction in an evidently equivalent or stronger form. Full theorem-level text of several older smoothing papers was not inspected end-to-end, leaving residual coverage risk.

value.summary: The result gives an exact explanation for unconditional early-step positivity after backward-Euler filtering on a canonical heat lattice, despite negative stiff-mode scalar amplification. It supplies a closed-form Green kernel, a reusable m>=k positivity certificate, and a sharp boundary-condition obstruction showing that the effect is not generic to all diffusion matrices.

limitations: The unconditional theorem is limited to the standard nearest-neighbor uniform one-dimensional heat lattice on Z or periodic cycles.
The condition m>=k is sufficient and is not claimed necessary.
No claim is made that a finite backward-Euler startup preserves positivity for every later Crank-Nicolson step.
A two-point homogeneous-Dirichlet grid fails positivity at s=1 even after two backward-Euler half-steps.
No extension is proved for arbitrary M-matrices, variable coefficients, nonuniform grids, finite elements, or higher-dimensional discretizations.
No new convergence-order, floating-point stability, efficiency, or optimal-timestep theorem is claimed.
Full theorem-level text of several historically relevant smoothing papers was not inspected end-to-end, leaving residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
